charrestore.theme.wilderness.npc.title: the wilderness guide
charrestore.theme.wilderness.npc.deflect: I am waiting for someone out on the trail. Move along, traveler.
charrestore.theme.wilderness.npc.lost_pa: I seem to have mislaid the pack I was carrying. Speak with the authorities.
charrestore.theme.wilderness.npc.confirm: Good. I knew it was you. Let me tell you how your gear came back to the road.
charrestore.theme.wilderness.npc.wrong_p: My apologies — wrong traveler. I will keep watching the paths.
charrestore.theme.wilderness.npc.farewel: Safe trails to you. Learn the wilds before they learn you.
charrestore.theme.wilderness.dialog.body: Hold there, traveler. Are you the one who was caught out on the wild paths — beasts, weather, or a bad camp? I have been carrying something that belongs to you. Tell me I have the right soul before I hand it over.

I thought as much. The wilds take plenty from the unprepared, but a sharp eye and quick hands can still win some of it back. I gathered what I could from the brush and the roadside before the scavengers did.

I have it bundled here. Ready to take it?

Here — your recovered gear. Take it all; the road owes you that much.

Advice from an old guide: know your landmarks before you wander. The wilderness does not forgive twice.
Thank you, guide. I will remember this.
charrestore.theme.ocean.npc.title: the sea salvager
charrestore.theme.ocean.npc.deflect: I am waiting for someone. Move along, traveler.
charrestore.theme.ocean.npc.lost_parcel: I seem to have lost the parcel I was carrying. Speak with the authorities.
charrestore.theme.ocean.npc.confirmed: Good. I knew it was you. Let me tell you how I came to have your things.
charrestore.theme.ocean.npc.wrong_person: My apologies for the confusion. I will keep looking.
charrestore.theme.ocean.npc.farewell: Safe harbors to you. Learn these waters before you venture out again.
charrestore.theme.ocean.dialog.body.gree: Hold there, traveler. Are you the one who was stranded by the sea's whim? I have been carrying something that belongs to you — or so I have been told. It would help me to know I have found the right person before I hand it over.
charrestore.theme.ocean.dialog.body.stor:
I thought as much. The sea gives and the sea takes — but sometimes a keen eye and quick hands can recover what the tides would claim. I pulled what I could from the wreckage before the current swept it away. Not every soul would bother, but I have seen too many good people lose everything to the waters. It is not right.

I have it all bundled here. Ready to receive it?
charrestore.theme.ocean.dialog.body.hand:
Here you are — your salvaged belongings. Take it all. It belongs to you, and the sea owes you at least this much.

A piece of advice from an old salvager: learn the coastlines before you sail them. The sea does not forgive twice.
charrestore.theme.ocean.dialog.btn.thank: Thank you, salvager. I will remember this.
charrestore.theme.dungeon.npc.title: the dungeon delver
charrestore.theme.dungeon.npc.deflect: I am waiting for someone who survived the depths. Move along.
charrestore.theme.dungeon.npc.lost_parce: The satchel I was carrying has gone missing. Seek the authorities.
charrestore.theme.dungeon.npc.confirmed: Good. I knew it was you. Let me tell you how I pulled your things from the ruins.
charrestore.theme.dungeon.npc.wrong_pers: Forgive me — not the delver I expected. I will keep searching the halls.
charrestore.theme.dungeon.npc.farewell: May your torch stay bright. Learn a dungeon before it learns you.
charrestore.theme.dungeon.dialog.body.gr: Hold, adventurer. Are you the one who lost everything to the halls below — traps, beasts, or a hasty retreat? I hold a bundle that bears your name. Confirm who you are before I release it.
charrestore.theme.dungeon.dialog.body.st:
So it is you. Dungeons swallow fortunes every day, yet sometimes a delver can still drag a satchel back from the rubble before the scavengers do.

I have your goods secured here. Ready to claim them?
charrestore.theme.dungeon.dialog.body.ha:
Take it — what the depths gave back. It is yours, and stone owes no apologies.

Heed an old delver: map your exits before you chase treasure. The dungeon does not forgive twice.
charrestore.theme.dungeon.dialog.btn.tha: Thank you, delver. I will remember this.
